name: C-comic-quest
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE high-fidelity desktop WEBSITE SCREENSHOT, 1536x1024 landscape, straight-on, edge to edge without browser chrome, device frame or external annotations. This is SproutLab, an existing English photosynthesis learning app for 10-year-old children. Redesign its active lesson screen, specifically the 'Your turn' phase of 'Sprout's food-making secret'. It is a usable children's learning activity, never a SaaS landing page, marketing page, dashboard, or poster. All text and controls must be large, crisp, correctly spelled and highly legible. Body text approximate 18–22px at this resolution, buttons at least 48px high. One dominant working visual and one obvious next action, compact navigation, very little prose. Show a coherent visual system an engineer could implement with semantic HTML buttons and SVG drawings. The central educational diagram MUST show a whole rooted plant with soil, connected stem and leaves; BLUE water travels INSIDE roots and stem to the leaf, never floating water droplets in air. A labeled magnified leaf slice may show chloroplasts, never a fantasy room or machine in a leaf. Sunlight provides energy. CO₂ enters through a tiny leaf opening. Sprout and Beep can appear as small supporting cartoon characters, with leaves rooted and robot outside the plant. No extra rewards, scores, new quizzes or timers. Show stop 2 of 7, and compact progression labels 'Story', 'Watch', 'Your turn' with Your turn active. Provide a 'Picture notes' link. Sound is optional. Keep the whole core activity and controls inside the screenshot. Avoid the rejected visual formula: warm cream canvas, forest-green chunky rounded headline, green pill navigation, lavender/yellow card grid, long title/subtitle masthead. No giant slogan, feature cards, testimonials, sign-up, pricing, gradient blobs, glassmorphism, gratuitous stickers or decorative dashboard statistics.
DIRECTION C — COMIC QUEST. A sophisticated playful children's science comic transformed into a web activity. Clean punchy graphic art, CHARCOAL ink #22283B, vivid LEMON YELLOW #FFE13B, CORAL #F7795D, clean WHITE, cyan water. True comic ink linework, a little restrained halftone only in illustration shadows; body text never textured. Type: energetic condensed bold display for SHORT headings and conventional highly legible humanist sans body; no bubble font, no cream, no green brand palette. Layout sharply different from garden scene and museum: a small yellow masthead 68px tall with custom compact SproutLab wordmark in charcoal, 'Map', 'Journal', '2 / 7' and 'Sound off'. Below it, a LEFT narrative strip occupying 26% width on coral ground and a RIGHT large white science work area 74% width, separated by a decisive dark vertical rule. In left strip show 'THE LEAF CASE' as a short compact heading, a cartoon of Beep the robot offering a sandwich to rooted Sprout, one short bubble from Sprout 'I make my own food!', then current task in simple clear text 'Your mission' and 'Follow water from the roots to the leaf.' with large black rectangular button 'Trace the water →'. One small label 'Story recap' establishes that it is narrative support. On right top bar are 'Story  /  Watch  /  Your turn' and 'Picture notes'. Hero is the INTERACTIVE DIAGRAM, not a heading: a large confidently inked plant rooted in a cutaway soil block occupying two-thirds of white area, blue dashed path visible inside the roots up the stem, a magnified leaf slice in the upper-right connected from a leaf, with chloroplasts. Playful anatomical labels 'Roots', 'Stem', 'Leaf', 'Inside the leaf' with tidy leader lines. A small sun at upper left casts clearly drawn rays on the leaf. Plant has botanical structure and no machinery. Along bottom of right work area a single horizontal task toolbar contains 'Water' with checkmark, 'Carbon dioxide' with a conventional button 'Let it in', and 'Sunlight' with a conventional slider. Bottom caption directly on white: 'Water travels inside the plant.' Only two or three large functional regions, NOT a grid of feature cards or decorative comic panels. Stage elements and controls have hard offset shadows of 3px at most, sharp or lightly eased corners, confident line weights. The result should feel like an original interactive science comic a 10-year-old would want to try, clear, energetic, age appropriate, not loud visual clutter.
